key_insight: B-VQE extends variational quantum eigensolvers to non-Hermitian many-body systems by using separate left/right circuits and a biorthogonal objective to detect exceptional points and phase transitions directly on NISQ hardware.
engineering_relevance: It offers a hardware-friendly route to map non-Hermitian phase diagrams without ancilla-heavy post-selection, making open-system and skin-effect physics more tractable on near-term quantum devices.
method: Uses independent variational circuits for left and right eigenstates of a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
Optimizes a biorthogonal loss with an Exceptional-Point Detector to locate eigenstate coalescence.
Adds NH-QGT readout and importance-sampling mitigation to reduce overhead and capture topological/critical signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on three benchmark models, with relative energy errors below 5×10^-3 on noise-free simulations and accurate exceptional-point localization.
watch_item: Results are reported primarily in noise-free simulation, so performance under realistic NISQ noise and scaling to larger interacting systems remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Exceptional-Point-Anchored Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Non-Hermitian Many-Body Phase Diagrams: Bridging Skin-Effect Topology and Entanglement Criticality on NISQ Hardware
